name: Luxury & Prestige
core_perception: A category where restraint is the proof of confidence. The audience reads visible effort to persuade as a downgrade, so the work must establish taste, provenance and rarity while appearing to explain almost nothing. Where a process must be shown, it is shown as craft, not as a feature list.
visual_traits: extreme space around a single subject
strictly controlled neutral palette or one decisive material colour
authored photography with material and light doing the work
communication_needs: establish taste level and provenance immediately
show material, finish and craft in enough detail to be judged
carry any required process or specification without breaking the restrained register
composition: Image-dominant with type used sparingly and exactly. Wide-margin restraint is the default; the uncommitted middle reads as retail. Where several steps or facts are mandatory, they are set as one quiet disciplined block rather than distributed as callouts.
typography: Minimal and confident, often very small, with wide tracking. A single wordmark can carry an asset. Explanatory copy weakens the register and is pushed to a secondary surface or a single restrained block.
color: Strictly controlled neutrals or a single decisive statement colour drawn from the material itself. Saturated brand colour and heavy contrast both read as mass-market.
imagery: Casting, styling, material and light carry the weight. Technical over-polish reads as commercial; texture, patina and atmosphere are assets.
avoid: Explanatory feature callouts, benefit bullets and promotional badges, which move the work into a retail register the audience discounts.
Dense layouts that carry every fact at once, which suppress the single strongest signal of rarity and craft.
Stock-feeling photography with generic casting or lighting, which destroys the taste signal faster than any layout error.
